messages:
maya: Quick sync — we need a tight checklist for GA entrance. Specifically: SLA language, docs parity (Hosted/Dedicated/Private), support handoff & oncall coverage, monitoring + runbooks, and pricing/burn-rate guardrails. Can owners confirm gaps by EOD?
chris: I'll take SLA + perf targets. Initial proposal: 99.9% monthly availability for hosted control plane, route-level latency targets: p50=50ms, p95=250ms for small-gen (<=256 tokens). Need perf runs on dedicated pool to validate.
sasha: I'll own monitoring + runbooks. Plan: dashboards for errors, latency, token burn; automated burn-rate alerts + paging rules. Need a clear error taxonomy from eng for meaningful alerts.
andrew: Pricing lead here — I'll draft tiered GA pricing and a burst-backstop policy. Need sample 7-day traffic profiles (tail / median). If anyone has 95th-percentile token counts, drop them here.
elaine: Docs owner. I'll produce: API quickstart, migration notes for Dedicated/Private parity, SLA page, and an ops runbook. ETA: first pass tomorrow noon. Need final SLA wording and any non-standard customer exemptions.
chris: Draft SLA blurb (for comments):
```
Redwood Inference will use commercially reasonable efforts to provide 99.9% availability for the Hosted API per calendar month. Availability measured at the control plane/API gateway level; exclusions include force majeure, scheduled maintenance (>=72h notice for major), and customer-managed network outages. Latency targets and throughput guidance are provided as operational targets and not part of the availability calculation.
```
please comment on the exclusions + measurement point.
sasha: +1 on exclusions. Suggest we explicitly call out regional failover behavior and fallback to alternative model variant when capacity constrained. Also: monitoring will emit these signals that feed SLA dashboards.
maya: @chris can you also say whether SLA measurement should be per-customer or global? Legal wants per-tenant clarity.
chris: Leaning to per-tenant for Dedicated and Private (since isolation), global for Hosted (same infra pool). We should call this out.
andrew: For pricing, propose 3 GA tiers: dev (low quota, free tier credit), standard (metered tokens), committed (monthly reserved capacity + discount). Add a burst/backstop add-on for short-term spikes — we'll need ops budget for that.
elaine: Docs question: do we publish the SLO probes and example curl checks? I can add a troubleshooting section with curl snippets and expected status codes. Example snippet:
```
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"model":"rwd-3b","input":"hello"}' | jq .
```
include expected latency ranges.
chris: Action: I'll run perf sweep on dedicated pool tonight and post p50/p95 results. If we miss targets, we'll flag as "needs optimization" not blocker for docs.
sasha: Action: I'll draft runbook and paging policy. Key decision: page on error-rate spike (>5% 5m), or on token burn anomaly (>2x expected 10m). Need agreement.
maya: Decision: for GA we page on severity=SEV2 for sustained errors affecting >5% customers OR sustained inability to accept new requests (backpressure) for >3 minutes. SEV1 reserved for total regional outage.
andrew: Action: I'll model revenue impact of burst-backstop and propose a charge/onboarding addendum for committed customers.
elaine: I'll sync docs examples with the billing team so customers see quota behaviour and error responses.
oncall-bot: Reminder: scheduled maintenance window Thursday 02:00-04:00 UTC — will be excluded from SLA.
maya: Gap check: anything missing? (auth edge cases, KMS/HSM for Private, or audit log retention)
sasha: Need explicit owner for audit log retention and KMS docs — @elaine to coordinate with security.
elaine: Will pull in security and add a separate Private deployment appendix.
maya: Great. Summarize owners and next steps:
- SLA & perf validation: chris (perf sweep + final wording)
- Monitoring & runbooks: sasha (dashboards + page rules)
- Pricing & burst policy: andrew (tier docs + model)
- Docs & deployment parity: elaine (API + runbooks + private appendix)
- Cross-check meeting: 16:00 UTC today to confirm EOD items.
If any blocker that prevents signoff, flag here. Otherwise we aim for GA gating doc to ship tomorrow morning. :white_check_mark:
maya: Thanks everyone — please drop final links to PRs/dashboards in the thread before 16:00.
chris: Uploaded perf artifacts: https://internal.redwood/ci/perf/1766543219 — p95 for small-gen = 230ms, p95 for long-gen (1k tokens) = 1.2s. I'll annotate anomalies.
andrew: Dropped a simple pricing sketch: https://notion.redwood/pricing/ga-sketch — ping me with scenarios.
sasha: Draft runbook PR: https://git.redwood/inference/runbooks/pull/342 — includes paging policy and alert thresholds.
elaine: Docs draft: https://docs.redwood.ai/drafts/ga-entrance — added curl examples and Private appendix.
maya: Perfect. We'll review at 16:00 and close owners. If all green, I'll add signoff to the GA gating doc and notify legal/sales.
chris: one more note — quantify expected cold-start memory pressure for dedicated pools so ops can size nodes. I'll add numbers to the perf artifact.
sasha: noted. Also adding a short playbook for failover to degraded-mode (restricting max tokens) to keep serving during capacity strain.
maya: That's it — thanks. :tada:
